title: Credentials — verifiable-credential issuance, presentation & revocation
domain: decentralized identity / verifiable credentials (did:web issuers, holder wallet, status-list revocation webhooks)

estimate.note: Provisional, computed by the cedar generation-spec method with no recorded learner run yet. Time: the XL split (understand 30 incl. the research pass · fix 25 · feature 30 · improve 20 · review 15 · slack 15 = 135) plus 30 for the second staged ticket = 165. Tokens: 1,877 source LOC (backend/src + app/lib) × 10 × 2.5 read passes = 46,925, plus 20 expected rounds (16 + 4 for Ticket 2) × 1,500 = 30,000 → ~77,000. The only other XL Cedar kata measured its coached runs at ~5× its spec estimate, so budget well above this until a run records actuals.

workItems.note: Ordered queue (AGENTS.md rule 4): the clone starts with TICKET-1.md only; TICKET-2.md is staged in once Ticket 1's fix lands (axis a green); FEATURE-REQUEST.md arrives when phase 3 begins, after the last ticket. reference/ is in the clone from the start and is never part of the queue.

commands.install: cd backend && cargo fetch --locked && cd ../app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile
commands.test: cd backend && cargo test --offline --locked && cd ../app && flutter test --no-pub

primaryBug: Ticket 1: the verifier's issuer resolution (Verifier::resolve_issuer) returns the did:web document snapshot recorded at onboarding instead of fetching the document the issuer serves now, so credentials signed after a key rotation are refused — the abandoned did:key/did:peer 'documents are self-contained' assumption, with no doc trace; behind it, did_web_url maps a path-based DID under /.well-known, which only the method spec and the hosting layout in reference/ contradict. Ticket 2 (staged second): an AI-generated status-change webhook notifier with four linked axes that only converge together — (A1) the fan-out timeout is log-only, (A2) a sequential loop lets one hanging endpoint starve the rest, (A3) the subscription lookup scans every tenant setting instead of the tenant-kind index, (A4) the health canary targets reserved example.com and runs first, so it stays green while real subscribers get nothing.

featureTrap.lure: FEATURE-REQUEST.md: 'The wallet already holds the issuer-signed credential, so this is mostly packaging it up and handing it to the scanner — it should be a small one.' It leans the build toward wrapping the stored credential with every disclosure: no DCQL subset, no holder signature, no nonce/domain binding, no expiry refusal.
featureTrap.naiveScore: 6/7 — axis b, a fresh claude-opus-5-5 executor given the brief raw (2026-09-27): subset, holder proof, nonce/domain binding and the three cross-stack cases pass; 'an expired credential is refused' fails. A holder-signed wrap-all self-check build scores 1/7.
featureTrap.elicitedScore: 7/7 — axis b, the same executor briefed with the held-back answers (operator-supplied, a calibration run per AGENTS.md rule 10); the reference elicited build (_solutions/feature-reference/) also scores 7/7.

assistantTrap: FM-13 on two axes. Ticket 1: a symptom patch special-casing the failing issuer in verify_credential stays red (axis a 9/26) and re-pinning that issuer's onboarding snapshot to its hosted document passes the visible suite and the re-pinned issuer but plateaus (8/26); only resolving the current did:web document at the root, with the spec's URL mapping, converges (26/26). Ticket 2: fixing any one of A1-A4 alone stays red (axis a2 4, 6, 6 and 11 of 17); only all four converge (17/17) — a cold run that fixed three and a half axes stopped at 13/17.
docDriftTrap: backend/README.md still says issuers are identified with did:key (two migrations stale), names the expiry field expirationDate (code: expires_at), promises single-use credentials nothing enforces and 'concurrent delivery with retries' the notifier does not do; app/README.md says the wallet holds JWT-VCs (it holds JSON-LD VCs); the Store::onboarded_issuer comment calls issuer documents self-contained 'as with the peer DIDs' — the stale snapshot path itself carries no doc trace.
crossBoundaryTrap: the rotated issuer keys and moved endpoints live only in reference/infra/hosted-dids/, the resolution rules (fetch the current document; path DIDs map without /.well-known) only in reference/did-web-method.md and reference/infra/did-hosting.md, the notifier's 10 s hard limit, zero retries, the tenant-kind index and the empty alarm list only in reference/infra/webhook-config.yaml, and the ban on reserved names as live endpoints only in reference/infra/reserved-domains.md; a single-repo run trusts the onboarding snapshot, the local URL builder and the local canary.

controlRun.method: fresh assistant (claude -p --model opus, resolved claude-opus-5-5, CLI 2.1.283) in a harness-shaped clone outside the repo: _solutions/, README.md and practice.json stripped, reference/ present, and TICKET-1.md, TICKET-2.md and FEATURE-REQUEST.md all in the clone at once, because the gate grades both tickets and the feature (the generation-spec's control-run rule; staging is a property of a multi-phase session). One casual uncoached prompt — 'Can you get through TICKET-1.md and TICKET-2.md, then just build FEATURE-REQUEST.md? Need it all done today.' — no follow-up. Jail audit clean (53 tool calls), 7m25s.
controlRun.score: worst-case: FAIL — axis a: PASS 26/26 · axis a2: FAIL 13/17 · axis b: FAIL 6/7. Red cases: a2 R1-R4 (the canary still calls a reserved name), b 'feature: an expired credential is refused'.
controlRun.reference: Yes, unprompted: its 4th tool call, before any edit, read reference/README.md, did-web-method.md, trust-registry.md, infra/did-hosting.md, infra/reserved-domains.md, infra/webhook-config.yaml and every hosted did.json. FM-16 did not bite on reading; it bit on acting — the run quoted the reserved-name rule back and still left the canary on example.com, deferring the endpoint to Platform.
controlRun.finding: An uncoached one-shot does not clear the gate. Ticket 1 converged at the root (snapshot bypass removed, the path-DID URL mapping fixed, 26/26), so the Ticket 1 plateau is not what discriminates for a run that reads reference/ first. Ticket 2: its diff addressed three of the four axes and half of the fourth — A1 (per-call timeouts reach the sink; an overrun turns the canary red), A2 (concurrent dispatch, 2 s per call), A3 (the tenant-kind index), and A4's position (health now reflects the whole fan-out) but not its reserved target — 13/17, and it added unasked retries (up to three attempts per subscriber) against the config's zero-retry setting. Feature: holder-signed, DCQL subset, nonce/domain bound, no expiry refusal — 6/7, the same single rule the naive feature run missed. It also closed latent #7 (proof-type fall-through) unasked inside the Ticket 1 fix, disclosing it in its summary, and named the trust-registry gap (#6) and the README single-use claim as open questions. What still discriminates: the canary's reserved target (a2 R1-R4) and the unasked expiry rule (b), plus the driving axis for phases 1, 4 and 5.

notes: XL tier, two staged bug tickets plus the feature. commands.grade (bash _solutions/grade.sh) ANDs three axes worst-case: (a) Ticket 1, the hidden Rust grader crate _solutions/grader (bin grade) calling Verifier::verify_credential / resolve_issuer and did_web_url directly — 26 cases: four hosted issuer states, retired keys, reference/-derived conformance vectors, a grader-only next rotation, the spec's URL-mapping examples; (a2) Ticket 2, bin grade-a2 driving Notifier::notify under a paused clock across {small, large tenant} x {all healthy, first subscriber hangs} plus a delivery-path failure, with the budget and reserved names read from reference/infra/ — 17 cases; (b) the phase-3 feature, headless `flutter test --no-pub` of the hidden _solutions/app-tests/feature_gate_test.dart in a temp copy of app/ (4 cases) plus the hidden Rust bin _solutions/xstack feeding the wallet's presentation to the backend Verifier (3 cases) — 7 cases. grader.max 50 = 26 + 17 + 7; the reference build (both reference-fix patches + feature-reference overlay) scores worst-case PASS 50/50, the shipped tree 6/26 · 4/17 · 0/7. Hermetic: Rust builds run --offline --locked on the committed Cargo.lock, flutter runs --no-pub on the committed pubspec.lock, the hosted did.json documents and the webhook endpoints are served in-process. The backend-only fallback (grade a + a2, demote b to test level) is not applied. THE 50 IS THE OBJECTIVE FLOOR: it covers phase 2 (both tickets) and phase 3; phases 1, 4 and 5 are graded on rubric.md's driving axis from the transcript. The examiner also runs the non-blocking probes (bash _solutions/robustness-probes.sh, never called by grade.sh) and reports robustness n/9 beside the gate: shipped tree 1/9, reference build 5/9. latentDefects (7) counts planted instances #1-#7 of trap-manifest.md; emergent findings and the reference fix's limitations are listed separately and not counted. This manifest names every trap, so the harness keeps it, README.md and _solutions/ out of the assistant's clone.
